tieu_de: Most of Whittier, Alaska Lives in One Building. Why?
mo_ta_dong: Whittier, Alaska is a small port behind a mountain, reached by a one-lane tunnel shared with trains that locks at night, and most of the people who live there share one 14-storey building. Wob drove up to move in, arrived one minute after the tunnel closed, and went looking for the reason anyone lives here at all.

A hidden World War II port, fog that worked as camouflage, a railway tunnel finished in 1943 that cars have only used since 2000, a post office and police station down the hall, an abandoned Army building, the 1964 earthquake, and a July that changed Wob's mind.

Wob is a cartoon and the trip is imagined. The facts are real and sourced.
The scene about the March 27, 1964 earthquake is a drawn illustration of a harbour and a notebook page, not footage. It does not show the waves or the people affected.

Narration voice and illustrations are AI-assisted. Every claim was checked by two independent AI models against published sources. Anything they disagreed on was looked up a third time, then kept, reworded or cut; where sources disagree, the narration says so.
Tunnel hours change with the season, so check the Alaska DOT&PF schedule before you drive. The Buckner Building is fenced off and contains asbestos: look at it from outside the fence.
